sentences.en: This is The Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 这里是《隐藏的大脑》。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: In this episode, we're going to talk about near-misses, almost, not-quites.
sentences.zh: 在本期节目中，我们将讨论“险些成功”、“差一点”和“未竟之事”。

sentences.en: First, we're going to talk about research that shows that coming close to winning something
sentences.zh: 首先，我们将讨论一项研究，它表明与成功失之交臂

sentences.en: can really affect your drive and motivation.
sentences.zh: 真的会影响你的动力和积极性。

sentences.en: You want to build that thing in that, hey, you're almost there.
sentences.zh: 你想营造出一种“嘿，你离成功只差一步”的感觉。

sentences.en: Then, my friend Daniel Pink will join us for a round of Stopwatch Science.
sentences.zh: 接下来，我的朋友丹尼尔·平克将加入我们，进行一轮“秒表科学”环节。

sentences.en: He's going to explain how the psychology of getting close to a goal can help charities raise more money.
sentences.zh: 他将解释接近目标的心理如何帮助慈善机构筹集更多资金。

sentences.en: Why do people give?
sentences.zh: 人们为什么捐款？

sentences.en: People give not because they want to be altruistic, but because they want to be effective.
sentences.zh: 人们捐款不是因为他们想表现得无私，而是因为他们想产生实际效果。

sentences.en: Finally, we'll ask singer-songwriter Casey Musgraves to put on an imaginary lab coat
sentences.zh: 最后，我们将请创作歌手凯西·马斯格雷夫穿上想象中的实验服，

sentences.en: and join us for a game of Mad ScientiSt.
sentences.zh: 加入我们的“疯狂科学家”游戏。

sentences.en: Does my lab coat have rhinestones on it?
sentences.zh: 我的实验服上镶有水钻吗？

sentences.en: We'll ask her to explain a song from her album Pageant Material,
sentences.zh: 我们将请她解释她专辑《选美材料》中的一首歌，

sentences.en: and we'll learn what world peace has to do with swimsuits.
sentences.zh: 并了解世界和平与泳装有什么关系。

sentences.en: Okay, near-misses.
sentences.zh: 好的，谈谈“险些成功”。

sentences.en: Monica Wadhwa is a professor at the INSEAD Business School in Singapore.
sentences.zh: 莫妮卡·瓦德瓦是新加坡欧洲工商管理学院的教授。

sentences.en: She studies marketing.
sentences.zh: 她研究市场营销。

sentences.en: And recently, in her research, she hit upon a strange but promising way to change how consumers behave.
sentences.zh: 最近，在她的研究中，她发现了一种奇怪但很有前景的方法来改变消费者的行为。

sentences.en: It's funny because this came from one of my childhood experiences, actually.
sentences.zh: 说来有趣，这其实源于我童年的一次经历。

sentences.en: To understand this idea, let's travel back in time to Monica's childhood.
sentences.zh: 为了理解这个想法，让我们回到莫妮卡的童年时代。

sentences.en: I was born and brought up in India, in Delhi.
sentences.zh: 我在印度德里出生长大。

sentences.en: Like many 13-year-olds, Monica had a craze.
sentences.zh: 像许多13岁的孩子一样，莫妮卡曾有过一种痴迷。

sentences.en: Now, her craze was somewhat unusual.
sentences.zh: 不过，她的痴迷有点不同寻常。

sentences.en: It was buying lottery tickets.
sentences.zh: 那就是买彩票。

sentences.en: As a child, I kind of wanted to have tons of money, right?
sentences.zh: 小时候，我特别想拥有很多钱，对吧？

sentences.en: So, and I was lazy.
sentences.zh: 而且我很懒。

sentences.en: So, lottery tickets was my answer to good life.
sentences.zh: 所以，买彩票是我通往美好生活的答案。

sentences.en: She played the lottery constantly.
sentences.zh: 她不停地买彩票。

sentences.en: I remember those days, we could buy lottery tickets.
sentences.zh: 我记得那些日子，我们可以买彩票。

sentences.en: There used to be stalls.
sentences.zh: 过去有专门的摊位。

sentences.en: You could just go get a lottery ticket for, I remember paying 10 rupees for it at that time.
sentences.zh: 你可以直接去买一张彩票，我记得当时是10卢比一张。

sentences.en: And you buy this lottery ticket.
sentences.zh: 你买了这张彩票。

sentences.en: And if you get like a certain set of numbers, if you get all of that correct, you could get a jackpot.
sentences.zh: 如果你中了一组特定的数字，如果全部对上，就能赢得大奖。

sentences.en: How many digits did it have?
sentences.zh: 有多少位数字？

sentences.en: I think it was six.
sentences.zh: 我想是六位。

sentences.en: So, you have to get the lottery sort of requires you to match all six digits to win the prize.
sentences.zh: 所以，彩票要求你必须匹配所有六个数字才能赢得奖金。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There was a problem, though.
sentences.zh: 不过有个问题。

sentences.en: Her dad worried that her passion for the lottery was distracting her from her schoolwork.
sentences.zh: 她父亲担心她对彩票的痴迷会让她无心学业。

sentences.en: A big exam was coming up, and he needed her to focus.
sentences.zh: 一场大考即将来临，他需要她集中注意力。

sentences.en: Not to mention, her habit was costing him a ton of money.
sentences.zh: 更不用说，她的习惯花了他一大笔钱。

sentences.en: But Monica kept buying lottery tickets until one day.
sentences.zh: 但莫妮卡一直买彩票，直到有一天。

sentences.en: When I insisted on getting more, he's like, no more.
sentences.zh: 当我坚持要买更多时，他说，不能再买了。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 到此为止。

sentences.en: You know, I don't know about you becoming a millionaire.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我不知道你能不能成为百万富翁。

sentences.en: I'm definitely going to get bankrupt.
sentences.zh: 但我肯定会破产的。

sentences.en: So, they worked out a deal.
sentences.zh: 于是，他们达成了一项协议。

sentences.en: Her dad would allow her to buy one last lottery ticket before the big exam, which she did.
sentences.zh: 她父亲允许她在考试前买最后一张彩票，她照做了。

sentences.en: And then she waited for the results.
sentences.zh: 然后她等待结果。

sentences.en: The results would come in a particular newspaper.
sentences.zh: 结果会刊登在特定的报纸上。

sentences.en: So, describe to me exactly what happened when that paper arrived that morning.
sentences.zh: 那么，请描述一下那天早上报纸送达时到底发生了什么。

sentences.en: Do you remember anything about the day at all?
sentences.zh: 你还记得那天发生的事吗？

sentences.en: I don't remember the exact thing.
sentences.zh: 我不记得具体细节了。

sentences.en: I just remember the emotions.
sentences.zh: 我只记得当时的情绪。

sentences.en: You know, I remember I was supremely excited.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我记得我当时超级兴奋。

sentences.en: You know, you kind of flip through and say, did I win it?
sentences.zh: 你知道，你翻看着报纸说，我中奖了吗？

sentences.en: Did I get it?
sentences.zh: 我中了吗？

sentences.en: Looking at the first, yes, it matched.
sentences.zh: 看第一个，是的，对上了。

sentences.en: Second, yes, it matched.
sentences.zh: 第二个，是的，对上了。

sentences.en: Third, yes, it matched.
sentences.zh: 第三个，是的，对上了。

sentences.en: And I'm just there.
sentences.zh: 我就在那儿。

sentences.en: I am going to be a millionaire in just about one second.
sentences.zh: 我马上就要成为百万富翁了，就在一秒钟之内。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Fourth one matched.
sentences.zh: 第四个也对上了。

sentences.en: And then the fifth.
sentences.zh: 然后是第五个。

sentences.en: Damn, it did not.
sentences.zh: 该死，没对上。

sentences.en: She loSt.
sentences.zh: 她输了。

sentences.en: I got my 10 rupees back.
sentences.zh: 我拿回了我的10卢比。

sentences.en: But the thing is, in that moment, 13-year-old Monica's emotions were not what you might expect.
sentences.zh: 但问题是，那一刻，13岁的莫妮卡的情绪并不是你所预想的那样。

sentences.en: She was actually happy.
sentences.zh: 她其实很开心。

sentences.en: I think I was feeling excited even after.
sentences.zh: 我想即使在那之后，我依然感到兴奋。

sentences.en: I was like, oh, hey, I almost got it.
sentences.zh: 我当时想，哦，嘿，我差一点就中了。

sentences.en: And so your reaction when you got four out of six, you were not dejected?
sentences.zh: 所以当你六个数字中了四个时，你的反应不是沮丧吗？

sentences.en: You were not, oh, my God, that was so close.
sentences.zh: 你没有觉得“天哪，太可惜了”吗？

sentences.en: I could have been so rich.
sentences.zh: 我本来可以那么有钱的。

sentences.en: And now I just get my 10 rupees back?
sentences.zh: 现在我却只拿回了10卢比？

sentences.en: It was kind of mixed feeling.
sentences.zh: 那是一种复杂的感觉。

sentences.en: You know, it was like, yes, there was a little bit of dejection.
sentences.zh: 你知道，就像是，是的，有一点点沮丧。

sentences.en: But maybe it's just me.
sentences.zh: 但也许只是我这样。

sentences.en: But there was a lot more excitement.
sentences.zh: 但更多的是兴奋。

sentences.en: I was an almost winner.
sentences.zh: 我是一个“准赢家”。

sentences.en: You know, I was almost there.
sentences.zh: 你知道，我离成功只差一步。

sentences.en: I got it.
sentences.zh: 我做到了。

sentences.en: How many people actually get almost there?
sentences.zh: 有多少人真的能做到“离成功只差一步”？

sentences.en: And this is where she surprised her dad and maybe even herself.
sentences.zh: 而这正是她让父亲甚至她自己感到惊讶的地方。

sentences.en: She didn't slack off before the exam.
sentences.zh: 她在考试前并没有偷懒。

sentences.en: I actually worked harder.
sentences.zh: 我反而更加努力了。

sentences.en: Really, I remember I was very excited for the exam because I just wanted to work much harder.
sentences.zh: 真的，我记得我对考试非常兴奋，因为我只想更加努力地学习。

sentences.en: Monica's best recollection of her performance in the exam?
sentences.zh: 莫妮卡对那次考试表现的最好回忆是什么？

sentences.en: I think I did well.
sentences.zh: 我想我考得不错。

sentences.en: Monica realized later that after she had nearly won the lottery, she had a strong, leftover urge to succeed, to do well at something, anything.
sentences.zh: 莫妮卡后来意识到，在差点赢得彩票后，她内心产生了一种强烈的、残留的成功渴望，想要在某件事上做得好，任何事都行。

sentences.en: Just the desire to get something.
sentences.zh: 仅仅是想要获得某种成就的渴望。

sentences.en: And that something happened to be the exam that it latched onto, I guess.
sentences.zh: 而那件事恰好就是她所投入的考试，我想是这样。

sentences.en: Fast forward a couple decades, and this childhood experience has now become the focus of Monica's academic research and marketing.
sentences.zh: 快进几十年，这段童年经历现在成了莫妮卡学术研究和市场营销的焦点。

sentences.en: When you get closer to a reward, your motivation intensifies as you approach the reward.
sentences.zh: 当你离奖励越近，你接近奖励时的动力就越强。

sentences.en: But when you miss it, you have this intensified motivational state, which is not satisfied now.
sentences.zh: 但当你错失它时，你会有一种增强的动机状态，而这种状态现在没有得到满足。

sentences.en: And our theory was that this intensified but not satisfied motivation will spill over and will make you seek other unrelated rewards now.
sentences.zh: 我们的理论是，这种增强但未满足的动力会溢出，并促使你现在去寻求其他不相关的奖励。

sentences.en: She and her colleagues recently tested this theory in a number of ways.
sentences.zh: 她和同事们最近通过多种方式验证了这一理论。

sentences.en: In one experiment, they recruited people to play a video game.
sentences.zh: 在一个实验中，他们招募了一些人来玩电子游戏。

sentences.en: We designed a game where they had to uncover some tiles, and if they uncovered eight diamonds, they could win a reward.
sentences.zh: 我们设计了一个游戏，他们必须揭开一些方块，如果揭开八颗钻石，就能赢得奖励。

sentences.en: By design, some people clearly won the game, some clearly lost, and then others...
sentences.zh: 根据设计，有些人明显赢了游戏，有些人明显输了，而其他人……

sentences.en: They missed the reward just by one diamond.
sentences.zh: 他们只差一颗钻石就赢得了奖励。

sentences.en: Monica wanted to know about that last group's almost win.
sentences.zh: 莫妮卡想了解最后一组“差点赢”的人。

sentences.en: Would that motivate them to seek another reward?
sentences.zh: 这会激励他们去寻求另一个奖励吗？

sentences.en: So we kind of secretly measured how much time, for example, it takes them to reach another reward, like a chocolate bar, which they could collect from another booth.
sentences.zh: 所以我们暗中测量了他们到达另一个奖励（比如可以从另一个摊位领取的巧克力棒）所需的时间。

sentences.en: People who nearly won, they walked much faster to get the chocolate.
sentences.zh: 那些差点赢的人，他们走得快得多去拿巧克力。

sentences.en: They were much more eager to get the second unrelated reward as compared to those who won or those who clearly loSt.
sentences.zh: 与那些赢了的人或明显输了的人相比，他们更渴望获得第二个不相关的奖励。

sentences.en: You actually had a chocolate bar at another station, and you actually measured how fast people took to walk to that second station?
sentences.zh: 你在另一个站点放了巧克力棒，并且测量了人们走到那个站点用了多快？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And your theory is that people were walking faster in some ways because they had nearly missed the first reward, and that put them in a state where they basically said,
sentences.zh: 你的理论是，人们走得更快，在某种程度上是因为他们差点错过了第一个奖励，这让他们处于一种状态，基本上就是说，

sentences.en: my desire for the next reward is even higher.
sentences.zh: 我对下一个奖励的渴望更高了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Turns out, the video game's near winners also salivated more when they stared at money, which I had to ask about.
sentences.zh: 事实证明，电子游戏中的“准赢家”在盯着钱看时也会分泌更多唾液，我不得不问这个问题。

sentences.en: What's the connection between salivation and watching money?
sentences.zh: 分泌唾液和看钱之间有什么联系？

sentences.en: You're not going to eat the money.
sentences.zh: 你又不会吃钱。

sentences.en: That is true, but salivation has been shown to be a measure of desire.
sentences.zh: 确实如此，但唾液分泌已被证明是衡量欲望的一种指标。

sentences.en: So when you desire something, you salivate more.
sentences.zh: 所以当你渴望某样东西时，你会分泌更多唾液。

sentences.en: In a second experiment, the researchers gave people lottery tickets outside a shopping mall.
sentences.zh: 在第二个实验中，研究人员在购物中心外给人们发彩票。

sentences.en: Again, the idea was that some people would win, some people would lose, and some would be near winners.
sentences.zh: 同样，这个想法是有些人会赢，有些人会输，有些人会成为“准赢家”。

sentences.en: The researchers then measured how much the near winners spent once they entered the mall.
sentences.zh: 研究人员随后测量了“准赢家”进入商场后的消费金额。

sentences.en: They spent a lot more than those who clearly lost or those who won.
sentences.zh: 他们比那些明显输了或赢了的人花得更多。

sentences.en: And this was like a really cool thing because from a marketing perspective, marketers think that winning will actually make them spend more.
sentences.zh: 这真是一件很酷的事情，因为从营销角度来看，营销人员认为获胜才会让他们花更多钱。

sentences.en: But this was just the other way around.
sentences.zh: 但事实恰恰相反。

sentences.en: Monica says the experience of nearly winning something can motivate people of all ages.
sentences.zh: 莫妮卡说，差点赢的经历可以激励所有年龄段的人。

sentences.en: I'm wondering if it has implications for things like parenting as well and management of people in a workforce.
sentences.zh: 我想知道这是否也对育儿和职场人员管理有启示。

sentences.en: I mean, so if you're trying to get your kid to practice the piano, for example,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，如果你想让你的孩子练习钢琴，例如，

sentences.en: in some ways sort of not getting the sticker from the teacher every week might actually be better than reliably getting the sticker every single week.
sentences.zh: 在某种程度上，每周没能从老师那里得到贴纸，可能比每周都能可靠地得到贴纸要好。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: If you get it each day every day, you are totally satiated.
sentences.zh: 如果你每天都能得到它，你就会完全满足。

sentences.en: You want to build that thing in that, hey, you're almost there.
sentences.zh: 你想营造出一种“嘿，你离成功只差一步”的感觉。

sentences.en: You're just there, but not quite there.
sentences.zh: 你就在那儿，但还没完全达到。

sentences.en: That's Monica Wadhwa, professor of marketing at the INSEAD Business School in Singapore.
sentences.zh: 以上是新加坡欧洲工商管理学院市场营销学教授莫妮卡·瓦德瓦。

sentences.en: After this break, we're going to be joined by my friend Daniel Pink for another round of Stopwatch Science.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，我的朋友丹尼尔·平克将加入我们，进行新一轮的“秒表科学”。

sentences.en: Back now for another round of Stopwatch Science.
sentences.zh: 现在回到“秒表科学”环节。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantam.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆。

sentences.en: And I'm Daniel Pink.
sentences.zh: 我是丹尼尔·平克。

sentences.en: Dan is our senior Stopwatch Science correspondent.
sentences.zh: 丹是我们“秒表科学”的资深通讯员。

sentences.en: He's also the author of several books about human behavior.
sentences.zh: 他也是几本关于人类行为书籍的作者。

sentences.en: On Stopwatch Science, Dan and I give one another 60 seconds to summarize interesting social science research.
sentences.zh: 在“秒表科学”中，丹和我互相给对方60秒时间来总结有趣的社会科学研究。

sentences.en: I'll run a stopwatch as Dan speaks, and here's the buzzer he's going to hear if he exceeds his time.
sentences.zh: 丹说话时我会启动秒表，如果他超时，他会听到这个蜂鸣声。

sentences.en: That's not the sound of a dinner gong, Dan.
sentences.zh: 那不是晚餐的锣声，丹。

sentences.en: That's a sound that says you need to stop.
sentences.zh: 那是告诉你需要停止的声音。

sentences.en: That's like a Chuck Berris gong show gong.
sentences.zh: 那就像查克·巴里斯《锣声秀》里的锣声。

sentences.en: You're off the stage.
sentences.zh: 你被赶下台了。

sentences.en: What's the sound of my buzzer, Dan?
sentences.zh: 我的蜂鸣声是什么样的，丹？

sentences.en: You're going to hear this sound right here.
sentences.zh: 你会听到这个声音。

sentences.en: A little bit of a Looney Tunes sound appropriate for this segment.
sentences.zh: 一点点《乐一通》的声音，很适合这个环节。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: That is a profoundly irritating sound, and I'm going to try and make sure I don't get to hear it.
sentences.zh: 那声音真是让人心烦意乱，我得尽量确保自己听不到它。

sentences.en: Our topic today is about near wins.
sentences.zh: 我们今天的话题是关于“差一点就赢”。

sentences.en: As you just heard, Monica Wadhwa found that getting close to a win can boost your motivation and drive.
sentences.zh: 正如你刚才听到的，莫妮卡·瓦德瓦发现，离胜利近在咫尺可以激发你的动力和干劲。

sentences.en: Dan and I are going to look at several other factors right now.
sentences.zh: 丹和我现在要看看其他几个因素。

sentences.en: Dan, if you're ready, your first 60 seconds starts now.
sentences.zh: 丹，如果你准备好了，你最初的60秒现在开始。

sentences.en: Well, those of us who've taken Psychology 101 probably remember the famous study that showed when a rat gets closer to food, the rat moves faster.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们这些学过心理学入门的人可能还记得那个著名的研究，它表明当老鼠离食物越近，它移动的速度就越快。

sentences.en: So this is a study from the Journal of Experimental Social Psychology asking the important question, what if someone else is the rat and something else is the food?
sentences.zh: 所以这是一项来自《实验社会心理学杂志》的研究，它提出了一个重要的问题：如果换成别人是那只老鼠，而别的东西是食物呢？

sentences.en: So what they did is they looked at charities.
sentences.zh: 他们研究的对象是慈善机构。

sentences.en: When do we make gifts to charity?
sentences.zh: 我们什么时候会向慈善机构捐款？

sentences.en: And they looked at donations to Kiva, the online charity, and they found, not surprisingly, that as people got closer to their stated goal, giving went dramatically up.
sentences.zh: 他们观察了在线慈善机构Kiva的捐款情况，不出所料，他们发现随着人们越来越接近既定目标，捐款额会大幅上升。

sentences.en: Then they also did a study where they simulated a kid named Sheila, and they said Sheila has two candy bars to sell to hit her quota versus 32 candy bars to sell to hit a quota.
sentences.zh: 然后他们还做了一项研究，模拟了一个叫希拉的孩子，他们说希拉有两根糖果棒要卖才能达到配额，对比有32根糖果棒要卖才能达到配额。

sentences.en: Not surprisingly, they gave more money when Sheila was only two away.
sentences.zh: 不出所料，当希拉只差两根就能完成目标时，人们捐的钱更多。

sentences.en: And this goes to really, why do people give to charity?
sentences.zh: 这确实触及了人们为什么会向慈善机构捐款的本质。

sentences.en: Some of it's to be altruistic and relieve negative emotions, but it's also so they can feel effective.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是为了利他主义和缓解负面情绪，但也是为了让他们感到自己能有所作为。

sentences.en: And that's what near wins do.
sentences.zh: 而这就是“差一点就赢”所起的作用。

sentences.en: All right, great.
sentences.zh: 好的，太棒了。

sentences.en: I hope my gong was effective.
sentences.zh: 希望我的锣声起到了作用。

sentences.en: It certainly got Dan to stop speaking.
sentences.zh: 它确实让丹停止了说话。

sentences.en: I think this is fascinating, though, Dan, because, of course, we all feel that as we get closer to the goal, it's actually attainable.
sentences.zh: 不过丹，我觉得这很迷人，因为我们当然都觉得，当我们离目标越近，目标就越是触手可及。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: What I think was interesting about this is that someone else was actually pursuing the goal.
sentences.zh: 我觉得有趣的是，实际上是别人在追求目标。

sentences.en: What you were doing is you were giving a little bit of a lift, and you're more likely to give that person some assistance when that person is nearing the goal.
sentences.zh: 你所做的是给予了一点点推动，当那个人接近目标时，你更有可能给那个人提供一些帮助。

sentences.en: Yeah, and public radio stations do this all the time.
sentences.zh: 是的，公共广播电台经常这样做。

sentences.en: Instead of saying our goal is $2 million, they say our goal for this segment is $60,000 because it makes people feel that they can actually get to that goal that's more attainable.
sentences.zh: 他们不说我们的目标是200万美元，而是说我们这一阶段的目标是6万美元，因为这让人觉得他们真的能达到那个更易实现的目标。

sentences.en: Well, our goal for this segment is to see if Shankar can do his study in 60 seconds, and his time starts right now.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我们这一阶段的目标是看看尚卡尔能否在60秒内完成他的研究，他的时间现在开始。

sentences.en: All right, so if you want to know how to motivate people, it's very important to ask where they are in the process of reaching their goal.
sentences.zh: 好的，如果你想知道如何激励人们，询问他们处于实现目标的哪个阶段非常重要。

sentences.en: Are they just starting out, or are they nearly on their way to the goal?
sentences.zh: 他们是刚开始，还是已经快要接近目标了？

sentences.en: Are they nearly at the win?
sentences.zh: 他们是否离胜利近在咫尺？

sentences.en: Very much like you're just saying, Dan.
sentences.zh: 这和你刚才说的非常像，丹。

sentences.en: C.G.
sentences.zh: 去改变彼此

sentences.en: Wong at the University of Texas at Austin recently published a paper in the Journal of Personality and Social Psychology that found that where you are in the process makes a big difference in your motivation.
sentences.zh: 德克萨斯大学奥斯汀分校的王（Wong）最近在《人格与社会心理学杂志》上发表了一篇论文，发现你在过程中的位置对你的动力有很大影响。

sentences.en: When we are in the early stages of a challenge, it's important to have multiple options.
sentences.zh: 当我们处于挑战的早期阶段时，拥有多种选择很重要。

sentences.en: If you hear there are six different ways you can give money to a public radio station, you're more likely to stay engaged in the pledge drive.
sentences.zh: 如果你听说有六种不同的方式可以向公共广播电台捐款，你更有可能继续参与认捐活动。

sentences.en: On the other hand, as you get close to the win, having more options turns into a hindrance.
sentences.zh: 另一方面，当你接近胜利时，拥有更多选择反而成了阻碍。

sentences.en: In one study, as a blood donation drive started to approach its final stages,
sentences.zh: 在一项研究中，当献血活动开始接近尾声时，

sentences.en: people were more likely to be willing to donate blood when they were given a single way to do so rather than given multiple ways.
sentences.zh: 人们在只有一种献血方式时，比有多种方式时更愿意献血。

sentences.en: So, in other words, at the early stages of a quest, having lots of options gives us a reason not to lose hope.
sentences.zh: 所以换句话说，在追求的早期阶段，拥有很多选择给了我们不失去希望的理由。

sentences.en: As you approach the win, having lots of options becomes a distraction.
sentences.zh: 当你接近胜利时，拥有很多选择就成了干扰。

sentences.en: Oh, you were out of options, but you came in right on time.
sentences.zh: 哦，你本来没选择了，但你刚好及时赶到。

sentences.en: Yeah, it's interesting.
sentences.zh: 是的，这很有趣。

sentences.en: We can think of it as kind of a motivational funnel.
sentences.zh: 我们可以把它看作是一种激励漏斗。

sentences.en: You start wide, then as you get closer and closer, you go narrow.
sentences.zh: 你从宽处开始，然后随着你越来越近，你变得越来越窄。

sentences.en: I love the funnel idea.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这个漏斗的想法。

sentences.en: Dan has reached the narrow end of his funnel because his next 60 seconds starts right now.
sentences.zh: 丹已经到达了他漏斗的窄端，因为他的下一个60秒现在开始。

sentences.en: Okay, so we've talked a lot about the positive elements of near wins.
sentences.zh: 好的，我们已经谈了很多关于“差一点就赢”的积极因素。

sentences.en: Let's talk about the dark side of near wins.
sentences.zh: 让我们谈谈“差一点就赢”的阴暗面。

sentences.en: And this is a study from the journal Neuron using two of my all-time favorite technologies, fMRIs, functional magnetic resonance imagers, and slot machines.
sentences.zh: 这是一项来自《神经元》杂志的研究，使用了我一直以来最喜欢的两项技术：功能性磁共振成像（fMRI）和老虎机。

sentences.en: And here's what they did.
sentences.zh: 他们是这样做的。

sentences.en: They put a bunch of participants in these fMRIs and had them play slot machines.
sentences.zh: 他们让一群参与者进入这些fMRI机器中，让他们玩老虎机。

sentences.en: But the slot machines, of course, were rigged, as all slot machines are, I guess.
sentences.zh: 当然，老虎机是被操纵的，我想所有的老虎机都是这样。

sentences.en: Sometimes the participants won, and a certain region of their brain was activated.
sentences.zh: 有时参与者赢了，他们大脑的某个区域就会被激活。

sentences.en: But then they had them lose, just by a hair.
sentences.zh: 但随后他们让他们输了，仅仅差一点点。

sentences.en: And you know what?
sentences.zh: 你知道吗？

sentences.en: The exact same region was activated.
sentences.zh: 完全相同的区域被激活了。

sentences.en: What?
sentences.zh: 什么？

sentences.en: So what happened is when they won, their brain said, let's play again.
sentences.zh: 所以发生的情况是，当他们赢的时候，他们的大脑说，再玩一次。

sentences.en: And then when they lost, they said, let's play again.
sentences.zh: 而当他们输的时候，他们说，再玩一次。

sentences.en: So this is the dark side of near wins.
sentences.zh: 这就是“差一点就赢”的阴暗面。

sentences.en: They almost have an addictive quality, which is why you should stay out of Vegas unless you bring your fMRI.
sentences.zh: 它们几乎有一种成瘾的特质，这就是为什么除非你带着你的fMRI，否则你应该远离拉斯维加斯。

sentences.en: I love the study, Dan, because actually it meshes so nicely with what Monica Wadhwa was talking about,
sentences.zh: 我喜欢这项研究，丹，因为它实际上与莫妮卡·瓦德瓦所谈论的内容非常吻合，

sentences.en: which is the effect of coming very close to a win is actually very similar in the brain to actually winning.
sentences.zh: 那就是离胜利非常近的效果，在大脑中实际上与真正获胜非常相似。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And you're very close to winning here because you have one minute for your next study, and it starts now.
sentences.zh: 而且你离胜利也非常近，因为你的下一项研究有一分钟时间，现在开始。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So this is one of my favorite studies on the science of motivation.
sentences.zh: 这是我最喜欢的关于动机科学的研究之一。

sentences.en: I talked about it with Steve Inskeep on Morning Edition some months ago.
sentences.zh: 几个月前我在《早间版》节目中和史蒂夫·英斯基普谈过它。

sentences.en: Max Ostinelli at the University of Wisconsin-Milwaukee, along with David Luna and Torsten Ringberg, they recently analyzed how movement can affect motivation.
sentences.zh: 威斯康星大学密尔沃基分校的马克斯·奥斯蒂内利，与大卫·卢纳和托尔斯滕·林伯格一起，最近分析了运动如何影响动机。

sentences.en: And they find that telling or showing people they are moving upward or downward can impair or increase their drive and motivation.
sentences.zh: 他们发现告诉或向人们展示他们是在向上还是向下移动，会削弱或增加他们的干劲和动力。

sentences.en: In one experiment, the researchers asked people to imagine riding up 20 floors in an elevator or riding down 20 floors in an elevator.
sentences.zh: 在一个实验中，研究人员要求人们想象乘坐电梯上升20层或乘坐电梯下降20层。

sentences.en: The volunteers are then given math puzzles to solve in three minutes.
sentences.zh: 然后志愿者们要在三分钟内完成数学谜题。

sentences.en: And what the researchers find is that the volunteers who imagine going down solved more math problems than volunteers who imagine going upward.
sentences.zh: 研究人员发现，想象向下移动的志愿者比想象向上移动的志愿者解决了更多的数学问题。

sentences.en: And the difference wasn't trivial.
sentences.zh: 而且这种差异并非微不足道。

sentences.en: It was a 30 percent difference.
sentences.zh: 这是一个30%的差异。

sentences.en: The researchers think this is happening because as you move upward, your self-esteem gets boosted.
sentences.zh: 研究人员认为这是因为当你向上移动时，你的自尊心得到了提升。

sentences.en: And when you feel better about yourself, you say, who cares?
sentences.zh: 当你对自己感觉更好时，你会说，谁在乎呢？

sentences.en: Why do I need to solve math problems?
sentences.zh: 我为什么要解数学题？

sentences.en: I feel pretty good already.
sentences.zh: 我已经感觉很好了。

sentences.en: So this study suggests, Dan, that the next time you and I sit down to record Stopwatch Science, instead of sitting on the fourth floor of NPR, we're going to go to the basement.
sentences.zh: 所以这项研究表明，丹，下次你和我坐下来录制《秒表科学》时，我们不去NPR的四楼，我们要去地下室。

sentences.en: I'm in.
sentences.zh: 我加入。

sentences.en: I'm in.
sentences.zh: 我加入。

sentences.en: Absolutely, absolutely fascinating.
sentences.zh: 绝对，绝对令人着迷。

sentences.en: And, of course, neither one of us has an overconfidence problem.
sentences.zh: 当然，我们俩都没有过度自信的问题。

sentences.en: So that should be a factor here.
sentences.zh: 所以这应该是一个因素。

sentences.en: I'm sure it doesn't affect us whatsoever.
sentences.zh: 我相信这完全不会影响我们。

sentences.en: But I'm hearing our producers say they're going to build a new basement in the studio.
sentences.zh: 但我听到我们的制片人说他们要在演播室建一个新的地下室。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: This has been another round of Stopwatch Science.
sentences.zh: 这是《秒表科学》的又一轮节目。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹瑟姆。

sentences.en: And I'm Daniel Pink.
sentences.zh: 我是丹尼尔·平克。

sentences.en: After this break, I have a special guest joining me in the studio, country music singer Casey Musgraves.
sentences.zh: 休息之后，我有一位特别嘉宾加入我的演播室，乡村音乐歌手凯西·马斯格雷夫斯。

sentences.en: Stay with us.
sentences.zh: 请继续收听。

sentences.en: Now we're going to introduce you to a new segment that we're calling Mad ScientiSt.
sentences.zh: 现在我们要向大家介绍一个新的环节，我们称之为“疯狂科学家”。

sentences.en: Our first victim, country music singer Casey Musgraves.
sentences.zh: 我们的第一个受害者，乡村音乐歌手凯西·马斯格雷夫斯。

sentences.en: Casey, thanks for joining me on The Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 凯西，感谢你加入我的《隐藏的大脑》节目。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你。

sentences.en: Casey was just upstairs at NPR to perform a Tiny Desk concert.
sentences.zh: 凯西刚才在NPR楼上表演了一场“小桌台”音乐会。

sentences.en: Her new album is called Pageant Material.
sentences.zh: 她的新专辑叫《选美材料》。

sentences.en: As I listened to the album, Casey, I told myself there is no possible way anyone has done social science research
sentences.zh: 当我听这张专辑时，凯西，我告诉自己，绝不可能有人做过社会科学研究，

sentences.en: that looks at the connection between world peace and wearing a swimsuit on a stage.
sentences.zh: 去探讨世界和平与在舞台上穿泳装之间的联系。

sentences.en: And wouldn't you know it, I was wrong.
sentences.zh: 你猜怎么着，我错了。

sentences.en: So it turns out I came by work out of Arizona State University that looks at how beauty pageant winners go on to win political office.
sentences.zh: 结果我发现了亚利桑那州立大学的一项研究，探讨了选美冠军如何继续赢得政治职位。

sentences.en: So between 2000 and 2010, something like 12% of all female governors elected in the United States were former beauty pageant contestants.
sentences.zh: 所以在2000年到2010年间，美国当选的女性州长中，大约有12%是前选美选手。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: And among them, of course, we have Sarah Palin, former governor of Alaska, beauty pageant contestant.
sentences.zh: 当然，其中就有萨拉·佩林，阿拉斯加州前州长，选美选手。

sentences.en: If John McCain had been elected president, she would be vice president today in all likelihood.
sentences.zh: 如果约翰·麦凯恩当选总统，她很有可能今天就是副总统了。

sentences.en: She might have been the front runner for president in 2016.
sentences.zh: 她可能在2016年就是总统候选人了。

sentences.en: And in 2017, she might have had her finger on the big red nuclear button.
sentences.zh: 而在2017年，她可能已经按下了那个巨大的红色核按钮。

sentences.en: Who knows?
sentences.zh: 谁知道呢？

sentences.en: So you tell me, Casey, can wearing a swimsuit on a stage have anything to do with world peace?
sentences.zh: 所以你告诉我，凯西，在舞台上穿泳装和世界和平有什么关系吗？

sentences.en: Maybe it's to do with the brain in the swimsuit.
sentences.zh: 也许这和泳装里的大脑有关。

sentences.en: I don't know.
sentences.zh: 我不知道。

sentences.en: Where did the idea for pageant material come from?
sentences.zh: 《选美材料》这个想法是从哪里来的？

sentences.en: So pageant material was written with two friends of mine, Luke Laird and Shane McAnally.
sentences.zh: 《选美材料》是和我两个朋友卢克·莱尔德和肖恩·麦卡纳利一起写的。

sentences.en: And Shane is from the South.
sentences.zh: 肖恩来自南方。

sentences.en: He's from Texas, as am I.
sentences.zh: 他来自德克萨斯州，我也是。

sentences.en: So we both kind of grew up in this area where that was a total normal thing.
sentences.zh: 所以我们都在那种完全正常的环境中长大。

sentences.en: You know, that was a thing girls really wanted to do.
sentences.zh: 你知道，那是女孩们真正想做的事情。

sentences.en: And he had this title.
sentences.zh: 他有这个标题。

sentences.en: He said, I really want to write a song called pageant material.
sentences.zh: 他说，我真的很想写一首叫《选美材料》的歌。

sentences.en: And I just thought I can totally get behind that.
sentences.zh: 我当时就想，我完全支持这个想法。

sentences.en: I mean, it's it's just like a lighthearted song.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就像一首轻松愉快的歌。

sentences.en: Just kind of poking fun at myself for not being, you know, maybe up to like industry pageant standards.
sentences.zh: 只是有点自嘲，因为我可能没有达到那种行业选美的标准。

sentences.en: And sometimes in the music industry, there's there's expectations for women to maybe act a certain way.
sentences.zh: 有时在音乐行业，对女性有一些期望，要求她们以某种方式行事。

sentences.en: And and I've found myself in certain situations where I don't come up to par with some of those things.
sentences.zh: 我发现自己在某些情况下，并没有达到那些标准。

sentences.en: And so when that happens, do you feel critical about yourself or do you say, look, these are silly social norms?
sentences.zh: 那么当这种情况发生时，你会对自己进行批判，还是会说，看，这些是愚蠢的社会规范？

sentences.en: I'm glad I'm actually not following them.
sentences.zh: 我很高兴我实际上没有遵循它们。

sentences.en: The latter, for sure.
sentences.zh: 当然是后者。

sentences.en: I mean, you know, I think there's always going to be people that are looking to find something wrong with what you're doing or, you know, picking you apart.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，你知道，我认为总会有人想找你做的事情的毛病，或者，你知道，对你挑三拣四。

sentences.en: But I think it's always best just to be yourself.
sentences.zh: 但我认为做自己总是最好的。

sentences.en: And if that means, you know, you're not smiling at a certain point or this or that, you know, if it's what you're feeling, you know, to a certain extent, I think you should do it.
sentences.zh: 如果这意味着，你知道，你在某个时候没有笑，或者这样那样，你知道，如果这是你的真实感受，你知道，在某种程度上，我认为你应该这样做。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So that's a great segue into our game.
sentences.zh: 这是一个很好的过渡，进入我们的游戏。

sentences.en: And so I'm going to tell you how we play Mad ScientiSt.
sentences.zh: 我要告诉你我们怎么玩“疯狂科学家”。

sentences.en: Social scientists are constantly coming up with crazy studies and experiments.
sentences.zh: 社会科学家不断地提出疯狂的研究和实验。

sentences.en: So on Mad Scientist, I'm going to tell you about a piece of social science research.
sentences.zh: 所以在“疯狂科学家”环节，我会告诉你一项社会科学研究。

sentences.en: And you put on your imaginary lab coat and try and deduce what the research experiment discovered.
sentences.zh: 然后你穿上你想象中的实验服，试着推断这项研究实验发现了什么。

sentences.en: Does that sound like a plan?
sentences.zh: 听起来是个好主意吗？

sentences.en: Does my lab coat have rhinestones on?
sentences.zh: 我的实验服上有水钻吗？

sentences.en: It does.
sentences.zh: 有的。

sentences.en: Since it's fictitious, it does.
sentences.zh: 既然是虚构的，当然有。

sentences.en: I think you get to pick the kind of lab coat you want.
sentences.zh: 我想你可以选择你想要的实验服类型。

sentences.en: So yours definitely has rhinestones.
sentences.zh: 所以你的那件肯定有水钻。

sentences.en: Perfect.
sentences.zh: 完美。

sentences.en: So in listening to your title song, Pageant Material, I was struck by a line in the song that talks about how you feel about being runner up.
sentences.zh: 在听你的同名歌曲《选美材料》时，我被歌里的一句歌词打动了，谈到了你对获得亚军的感受。

sentences.en: God bless the girls who smile and hug when they're called out as a runner up on TV.
sentences.zh: 上帝保佑那些在电视上被叫到名字获得亚军时还能微笑拥抱的女孩。

sentences.en: I wish I could, but I just can't wear a smile and a smile.
sentences.zh: 我希望我能做到，但我就是无法一直带着微笑。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So here's the experiment.
sentences.zh: 那么实验是这样的。

sentences.en: Many years ago, Thomas Gilovich, who is a psychologist at Cornell University,
sentences.zh: 多年前，康奈尔大学的心理学家托马斯·吉洛维奇，

sentences.en: he and his colleagues collected videotape of all the silver and bronze medal winners at the 1992 Barcelona Olympics.
sentences.zh: 他和他的同事收集了1992年巴塞罗那奥运会上所有银牌和铜牌得主的录像带。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So the video clips showed the immediate reactions, the first reactions when athletes discovered they had won either silver or bronze.
sentences.zh: 视频片段展示了运动员在得知自己获得银牌或铜牌时的即时反应，也就是最初的反应。

sentences.en: Now, here's the question, and I want you to think it through aloud.
sentences.zh: 现在，问题来了，我希望你能大声思考一下。

sentences.en: We all know that winning silver is better than winning bronze.
sentences.zh: 我们都知道拿银牌比拿铜牌好。

sentences.en: Coming in second is better than coming in third.
sentences.zh: 第二名比第三名好。

sentences.en: When Gilovich and his colleagues examined the videos, do you think they found that the silver medal winners looked happier than the bronze medal winners?
sentences.zh: 当吉洛维奇和他的同事们研究这些视频时，你认为他们发现银牌得主看起来比铜牌得主更开心吗？

sentences.en: Or did they find that the bronze medal winners looked happier than the silver medal winners?
sentences.zh: 还是他们发现铜牌得主看起来比银牌得主更开心？

sentences.en: Can I ask you questions?
sentences.zh: 我可以问你问题吗？

sentences.en: You certainly can.
sentences.zh: 当然可以。

sentences.en: Where's the gold winner in this?
sentences.zh: 那金牌得主去哪了？

sentences.en: The gold winner is off jumping exuberantly.
sentences.zh: 金牌得主正在旁边兴奋地跳跃呢。

sentences.en: So he's already been announced.
sentences.zh: 所以他已经被宣布获奖了。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: He or she has been announced, and he's jumping up and down.
sentences.zh: 他或她已经被宣布获奖，正在那儿蹦蹦跳跳的。

sentences.en: But this experiment is only looking at silver and bronze medal winners.
sentences.zh: 但这个实验只观察银牌和铜牌得主。

sentences.en: Well, I can't help but feel like this is a massive trick.
sentences.zh: 好吧，我忍不住觉得这肯定是个巨大的陷阱。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: Of course not.
sentences.zh: 当然不是。

sentences.en: Well, dang, I would say obviously silver because it's a higher rank, but maybe even knowing that you got bronze and you're not totally out, man, this is a hard one.
sentences.zh: 好吧，该死，我会说显然是银牌，因为它的排名更高，但也许知道自己拿了铜牌，而且没有彻底出局，天哪，这真是一个难题。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: So I'm going to give you a clue.
sentences.zh: 那我给你一个提示。

sentences.en: The clue has to do with who you're comparing yourself against, that our happiness levels and our satisfaction with what we get in life is often not just tied to what we have,
sentences.zh: 这个提示与你将自己与谁进行比较有关，我们对生活的幸福感和满足感往往不仅取决于我们拥有什么，

sentences.en: but it's often tied in comparison to what other people have.
sentences.zh: 还往往取决于我们与他人拥有的东西进行的比较。

sentences.en: So who does a silver medal winner compare himself or herself to, and who does a bronze medal compare himself or herself to, and that's the clue to the answer.
sentences.zh: 那么银牌得主会将自己与谁比较，铜牌得主又会将自己与谁比较，这就是答案的线索。

sentences.en: Oh, yeah.
sentences.zh: 哦，对了。

sentences.en: So maybe there's a bigger letdown with silver comparing themselves to the ultimate winner, but there's more joy in a bronze winner knowing that they're not a loser at all.
sentences.zh: 所以银牌得主在与最终赢家比较时可能会有更大的失落感，而铜牌得主因为知道自己并没有彻底输掉比赛，反而会有更多的快乐。

sentences.en: So that's your answer?
sentences.zh: 所以这就是你的答案？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Casey Musgraves, you are correct.
sentences.zh: 凯西·马斯格雷夫斯，你答对了。

sentences.en: Yay!
sentences.zh: 耶！

sentences.en: You have won, Mad ScientiSt.
sentences.zh: 你赢了，疯狂科学家。

sentences.en: Can I keep my lab coat?
sentences.zh: 我可以保留我的实验服吗？

sentences.en: I think you have to return the lab coat.
sentences.zh: 我想你得把实验服还回来。

sentences.en: NPR holds on to all the rhinestone lab coats, I'm afraid.
sentences.zh: 恐怕NPR要收回所有的水钻实验服。

sentences.en: It's just company policy.
sentences.zh: 这是公司规定。

sentences.en: I'm wondering if this actually tells you anything about your own life.
sentences.zh: 我在想，这是否真的能让你了解自己的生活。

sentences.en: You know, the idea that when you compare yourself, who you're comparing yourself to actually determines how happy you're going to be.
sentences.zh: 你知道，当你进行比较时，你比较的对象实际上决定了你会变得多快乐。

sentences.en: And it makes no sense that bronze medal winners would compare themselves against people who were the total losers and therefore felt happy.
sentences.zh: 铜牌得主会把自己与那些彻底失败的人进行比较，从而感到快乐，这听起来似乎没道理。

sentences.en: And the silver medal winners compared themselves to the gold and they felt unhappy.
sentences.zh: 而银牌得主把自己与金牌得主进行比较，所以感到不快乐。

sentences.en: But that's exactly what Gilovich and his colleagues found.
sentences.zh: 但这正是吉洛维奇和他的同事们所发现的。

sentences.en: That's so crazy.
sentences.zh: 那太疯狂了。

sentences.en: Recently, and I think it was, I'm going to get this wrong, but comparison is the ultimate thief of joy.
sentences.zh: 最近，我想是这样，我可能会记错，但比较是快乐的终极窃贼。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Something like that.
sentences.zh: 差不多就是这样。

sentences.en: Because there are always going to be people who have more than you.
sentences.zh: 因为总会有人比你拥有更多。

sentences.en: And there will always be people who have less than you.
sentences.zh: 也总会有人比你拥有更少。

sentences.en: And so you constantly go through life comparing ourselves to all these people and then feeling these silly aspects of happiness.
sentences.zh: 所以我们不断地在生活中将自己与这些人进行比较，然后产生这些愚蠢的幸福感。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Some void when it's like, if you could just look at yourself instead, you might come away way more happy.
sentences.zh: 当这种空虚感出现时，如果你能转而审视自己，你可能会感到快乐得多。

sentences.en: Wonderful.
sentences.zh: 太棒了。

sentences.en: That's Casey Musgraves.
sentences.zh: 那是凯西·马斯格雷夫斯。

sentences.en: Her new album is called Pageant Material.
sentences.zh: 她的新专辑叫《选美材料》。

sentences.en: Casey, thank you for playing Mad Scientist with me on The Hidden Brain.
sentences.zh: 凯西，谢谢你和我一起在《隐藏的大脑》节目中玩“疯狂科学家”游戏。

sentences.en: Thanks for the challenge.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你的挑战。

sentences.en: To hear more Casey Musgraves, check out her Tiny Desk concert at NPR Music.
sentences.zh: 想听更多凯西·马斯格雷夫斯的音乐，请查看她在NPR音乐频道的“小桌子”音乐会。

sentences.en: For more Hidden Brain, join us on Facebook and Twitter and listen to my NPR stories on your local public radio station.
sentences.zh: 想了解更多《隐藏的大脑》，请在Facebook和Twitter上关注我们，并在当地公共广播电台收听我的NPR报道。

sentences.en: The Hidden Brain podcast is produced by Cara McGurk-Allison and Maggie Penman.
sentences.zh: 《隐藏的大脑》播客由卡拉·麦格克-艾利森和玛吉·彭曼制作。

sentences.en: Special thanks this week to Chris Benderev, Bob Boylan, and Jacob Ganz.
sentences.zh: 本周特别感谢克里斯·本德列夫、鲍勃·博伊兰和雅各布·甘兹。

sentences.en: I'm Shankar Vedantham, and this is NPR.
sentences.zh: 我是尚卡尔·维丹塔姆，这里是NPR。
